fix(server): the 20% damage scroll stacks with the attack-up buffs (#4382)

Fixes #4382.

## What players see
With the 20% damage scroll active, the Chinese fire attack-up (`SKILL_CH_FIRE_GONGUP_*`) and lightning attack-up (`SKILL_CH_LIGHTNING_GWANTONG_*`) buffs were refused, and the scroll was refused under them. Now they stack in either order. The quest and event damage-up buffs still refuse the scroll and both attack-up buffs, as on later retail.

## Why
The native buff admission refuses a buff whose casting states (skilldata column 19, up to three state bytes) an active effect already holds. The rule is unchanged; only the input differs by era:

| Source | `SKILL_MALL_DAMAGE_INC_20P_SCROLL_01` | Quest damage-up (`SKILL_ETC_GNGWC_DAMAGE_UP_20_01` and 12 `SKILL_QNO_*`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| v1.150 client data (shipped) | 5, 4 | 5, 4 |
| vSRO v1.188 `server_dep` | 94, 5, 4 | 94, 5, 4 |
| ISRO-R shard backup, later DB-to-media dumps | **94** | 94, 5, 4 |

The owner adopted the later revision (2026-11-25, in chat: "yes so they stack but use common sense"). A later native client counts as native, so this is the native default with no flag.

## Change
- `enterworld/skillstates.go` (new): `laterPackedStates`, the 14 rows of the 20% damage family with their later column 19, and `packedStatesFor`.
- `enterworld/skilldata.go`: the one `compileSkillReplacement` call site applies `packedStatesFor`. `skillreplacement.go` itself is pinned by native evidence and is untouched.
- Every other row keeps its v1.150 value. The 20% damage-absorb scroll (10, 9) is the same in every source.

The one compile site feeds both the server admission and the skill catalogue's `SkillUiReplace.States`, which the client's press admission reads, so client and server agree.

## Native claims

| Claim | Evidence | How checked | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The admission refuses a buff whose column-19 states an active effect holds | The v1.188 server's buff replacement and casting-state conflict check; the port's `statuseffect.CastingConflictSnapshot` | Read in the server binary | Checked |
| The later retail scroll holds state 94 alone; the quest damage-up buffs hold 94, 5, 4 | The ISRO-R shard backup and the DB-to-media `server_dep` skilldata | Read the rows (author-reported: the backup is private) | Checked |
| The fire and lightning attack-up buffs hold 4 and 5 in every source | All three sources above | Read the rows | Checked |

## Tests
- `TestDamageScrollAndAttackUpStack` (it replaces #671's `TestDamageScrollAndAttackUpRefuseEachOther`): scroll then buff, and buff then scroll, both install, and the scroll is spent once.
- `TestDamageFamilyKeepsTheLaterRetailConflicts`: the shipped rows through the conflict check. The scroll is free of both attack-up buffs, and the quest damage-up buff refuses the scroll and both.
- Mutation: with `packedStatesFor` returning column 19 unchanged, both tests fail.
- `go test ./internal/game/enterworld` passes. `./internal/game/action` passes except `TestStyriaDoneWhenHunterAndThief`, which fails on the shared built item data (the reward items #4399 merged are not built in yet); it is unrelated.

Old-tab: safe - server data only; no wire or client change.

new file mode 100644
index 000000000..dd92e2333
--- /dev/null
+++ b/apps/server/internal/game/enterworld/skillstates.go
@@ -0,0 +1,64 @@
+/*
+===========================================================================
+
+skillstates.go - the later retail casting states of the 20% damage buffs
+
+Skilldata column 19 packs up to three casting-state bytes. The native buff
+admission refuses a buff whose states an active effect already holds
+(its casting-state conflict check), so the column decides which buffs
+stack. The v1.150 client's data gives the 20% damage scroll states 5 and 4,
+the same as the Chinese lightning (5) and fire (4) attack-up buffs, so the
+scroll and those buffs refuse each other.
+
+A later retail revision moved the 20% damage family onto its own state 94
+(the ISRO-R shard backup and the later DB-to-media dumps): the Mall scroll
+holds 94 alone and stacks with the attack-up buffs; the quest and event
+damage-up buffs hold 94, 5 and 4, so they still refuse the attack-up buffs
+and the scroll. The owner adopted that revision (2026-11-25, #4382; a later
+native client is native). This table gives those rows their later value and
+leaves every other row as the v1.150 data says.
+
+===========================================================================
+*/
+
+package enterworld
+
+// damageFamilyState is the later retail state every 20% damage buff holds.
+const damageFamilyState = 94
+
+// damageFamilyAttackStates are states 94, 5 and 4: the family's own state
+// plus the attack-up buffs' states, which those rows keep.
+const damageFamilyAttackStates = damageFamilyState | 5<<8 | 4<<16
+
+// laterPackedStates maps a codename to its later retail column 19.
+var laterPackedStates = map[string]uint32{
+	"SKILL_MALL_DAMAGE_INC_20P_SCROLL_01": damageFamilyState,
+	"SKILL_ETC_GNGWC_DAMAGE_UP_20_01":     damageFamilyAttackStates,
+	"SKILL_QNO_CA_GORIA_6_01_01":          damageFamilyAttackStates,
+	"SKILL_QNO_CA_GORIA_6_03_01":          damageFamilyAttackStates,
+	"SKILL_QNO_CH_GENARAL_1_01_01":        damageFamilyAttackStates,
+	"SKILL_QNO_CH_HWAN_1_4_04_01":         damageFamilyAttackStates,
+	"SKILL_QNO_CH_SPECIAL_2_02_01":        damageFamilyAttackStates,
+	"SKILL_QNO_CH_WHAN_2_1_01_01":         damageFamilyAttackStates,
+	"SKILL_QNO_EU_EASTEU_14_02_01":        damageFamilyAttackStates,
+	"SKILL_QNO_EU_EASTEU_21_02_01":        damageFamilyAttackStates,
+	"SKILL_QNO_EU_GENERAL_1_01_01":        damageFamilyAttackStates,
+	"SKILL_QNO_EU_IVY_2_01_01":            damageFamilyAttackStates,
+	"SKILL_QNO_EU_WHAN_2_1_01_01":         damageFamilyAttackStates,
+	"SKILL_QNO_WC_WAREHOUSE_W_2_04_01":    damageFamilyAttackStates,
+}
+
+/*
+================
+packedStatesFor
+
+The casting states a skill row admits with: the later retail value for the
+20% damage family, else the row's own column 19.
+================
+*/
+func packedStatesFor(codename string, column uint32) uint32 {
+	if later, ok := laterPackedStates[codename]; ok {
+		return later
+	}
+	return column
+}

benchmarks.task_description:
Fix CloudFront hosted_zone_id for AWS European Sovereign Cloud

<!-- Copyright IBM Corp. 2014, 2026 -->
<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MPL-2.0 -->

<!---
See what makes a good Pull Request at: https://hashicorp.github.io/terraform-provider-aws/raising-a-pull-request/
--->

<!-- heimdall_github_prtemplate:grc-pci_dss-2024-01-05 -->

## Changes to Security Controls

No changes to security controls (access controls, encryption, logging).

### Description

In the AWS European Sovereign Cloud partition (`aws-eusc`, region `eusc-de-east-1`), Route 53 alias records that target a CloudFront distribution must use hosted zone ID `Z02010231DDS20FNRTLEC`.

`CloudFrontDistributionHostedZoneID` only special-cased China (`aws-cn` → `Z3RFFRIM2A3IF5`) and returned the commercial ID `Z2FDTNDATAQYW2` for every other partition. In `aws-eusc`, using `aws_cloudfront_distribution.hosted_zone_id` as an alias target therefore fails (provider v6.74.0):

```text
Error: creating Route53 Record: operation error Route 53: ChangeResourceRecordSets, https response error StatusCode: 400, RequestID: ..., InvalidChangeBatch: [RRSet with DNS name example.com., type A contains an alias target that contains a hosted zone Z2FDTNDATAQYW2 that is an invalid alias target.]
```

This change adds an `aws-eusc` case (via `endpoints.AwsEuscPartitionID`) returning `Z02010231DDS20FNRTLEC`, consistent with the China precedent and the [AWS European Sovereign Cloud Route 53 docs](https://docs.aws.eu/esc/latest/userguide/route53.html). `aws_cloudfront_distribution` (resource and data source), API Gateway domain names and Cognito user pool domains already use the shared helper, so no call-site changes are needed.

### Relations

Relates #15223 (China precedent, fixed in #21943)

### References

* https://docs.aws.eu/esc/latest/userguide/route53.html
* https://docs.amazonaws.cn/en_us/aws/latest/userguide/route53.html
* https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws/issues/15223
* https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws/pull/21943

### Output from Acceptance Testing

Unit tests; manually verified the alias works in aws-eusc with the corrected zone ID.

```console
% go test ./internal/conns/ -run TestAWSClientCloudFrontDistributionHostedZoneID -v
--- PASS: TestAWSClientCloudFrontDistributionHostedZoneID (0.00s)
    --- PASS: .../AWS_Commercial (0.00s)
    --- PASS: .../AWS_China (0.00s)
    --- PASS: .../AWS_European_Sovereign_Cloud (0.00s)
```

benchmarks.task_description:
Let JWKS verifiers accept AWS KMS pipeline signatures

## Description

`--verification-jwks-file` rejects KMS-signed steps even when the file contains the right public key, because the signature has no key ID. The agent now puts the KMS key ARN in the protected `kid` header whether `--signing-aws-kms-key` names a key ID or an alias. Use that ARN as the public key's `kid` in the file. If an alias moves between lookup and signing, the agent returns an error rather than a signature with the wrong key ID.

## Context

When a team moves pipeline signing from a self-managed key to AWS KMS, its agents still need to verify steps signed with either key. Keeping both public keys in the local JWKS lets those agents enforce verification throughout the switch without needing AWS access.

[go-pipeline v0.19.1](https://github.com/buildkite/go-pipeline/releases/tag/v0.19.1) includes [the change](https://github.com/buildkite/go-pipeline/pull/97) that lets the KMS signer supply its key ID.

## Public documentation

**Status:** hold: Document, but do not publish yet

## Testing

- [x] Ran `GOWORK=off go test ./...` locally. The KMS tests passed for a key ID, an alias, and alias reassignment. Two unrelated macOS tests failed locally: `TestVerifyCommit` and `TestPluginCacheAcrossJobs`. Both also failed on the unchanged base.
- [x] Changed Go files formatted with `gofumpt -extra`.

## Disclosures / Credits

Me + Amp
